evidence.claim: Daily bullish engulfing sets long priority; price reacts at an FVG plus prior consolidation/volume-profile overlap, breaks a lower-timeframe downtrend line, and the nearby bearish engulfing OB is treated as the first resistance/exit area.
A completed five-minute bearish engulfing zone is treated as nearby resistance; the trader plans full profit and breakeven protection rather than forcing a distant fixed-R target.
FVG plus SR-flip support is used for a long; stop is the small-wave origin whose loss would change the local structure.
The next order-block resistance is used for a partial, and the stop is raised only after a new low/high structure forms.

After displacement creates an FVG, the trader waits for a retracement and cancels rather than chases when the desired price is not offered; a later lower-timeframe trend break and bullish OB reaction creates another entry.
Timeframe overlap is explicit: daily/weekly for the large trend, 12h/4h/1h for intermediate trend and support/resistance, and 15m/5m/1m for execution.
A trend-line breakout and retest creates a double-engulfing bullish order block; entry is taken around the support zone with the stop at the OB low until structural invalidation.
The first known high/liquidity is used for a partial even when nominal RR is below 1; the remainder is managed dynamically rather than by a mandatory fixed-R target.
The transcript explicitly rejects forcing a fixed RR and prefers taking available profit at expected resistance.
A completed five-minute first OB after a new low can shorten risk; after partial profit, the final structural stop may be retained rather than moved mechanically to breakeven.
A pre-existing 15-minute FVG resistance is used as the full intraday exit because the original intent was a day trade.
